transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-18 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Ari Singh (ZenPath CTO), Priya Rao (ZenPath ML Lead), Tom Becker (ZenPath Eng Manager)

Auto-summary: Short scoping call to align on models to bench for ZenPath's legal due-diligence POC (EN/FR/DE), define perf targets and dataset needs, and agree next steps for a 48hr benchmark run in ZenPath's VPC.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, that's Diego our solutions eng. Quick intros?
[00:12] Ari: Hey, Ari here, CTO at ZenPath.
[00:15] Priya: Priya, ML lead.
[00:17] Tom: Tom, engineering manager.
[00:20] Diego: Great. Goal today is pick a small set of open models to validate for accuracy and cost tradeoffs, and lock success criteria and infra constraints.

[00:38] Maya: Quick context from our side — you told us in the form you need legal due-diligence summarization and clause extraction across English, French and German, with high precision on obligation statements. Correct?
[00:47] Priya: Yeah, exactly. We care a lot about false positives on obligations — that kills downstream legal workflows.
[00:52] Ari: Also data has PII and contracts sometimes have bank numbers and client info. So we need strong controls: VPC/private deployment, KMS for keys, and audit logs.

[01:05] Diego: Understood. That steers us towards models we can run in Private (VPC) or on Dedicated infra. We'll propose both hosted runs for quick evaluation and a private benchmark in your environment for final validation.

[01:32] Tom: Budget question up front: we have a rough monthly cap for inference of $Xk, but for POC we want to keep per-token costs low while we iterate.
[01:40] Maya: Totally fair. So we'll include cost estimates for token-level cost across the shortlist.

[02:00] Priya: For success metrics — what are realistic thresholds? We're thinking exactness: precision > 92% on obligations, recall > 85% maybe? Latency P95 under 1.2s for single-document summarize flow is ideal.
[02:15] Diego: That's reasonable. Clarify doc sizes: average doc length?
[02:20] Priya: Average 1.5k tokens, heavy tails up to 6k from some contracts.

[02:35] Diego: Okay that affects batch vs streaming. If many docs are long we need model variants with good long-context handling or efficient chunking + KV cache. We'll measure end-to-end latencies on your average doc length in the bench.

[03:00] Maya: Workload sizing — what's expected throughput for POC? QPS / concurrency?
[03:05] Tom: For the POC baseline, ~40 concurrent requests at peak, burst to 120 for short windows. Day-to-day: ~12k docs/day.

[03:20] Diego: Good. That maps to approx 18M tokens/day (back-of-envelope) given your avg. We'll propose a Dedicated pool config and a hosted option. For bench we can emulate bursty traffic.

[03:44] Priya: Multilingual quality: we need models that are trained or finetuned with FR/DE data. Some smaller models are poor in German.
[03:52] Maya: Right — our shortlist will include candidates we know have multilingual coverage plus fine-tune-friendly ones.

[04:10] Ari: Can you list specific models you intend to bench? We prefer open weights.
[04:15] Diego: Preliminary candidates — (1) Llama-3 13B instruction-tuned variant (quantized int8), (2) Mistral Mix-9B (or Mistral 7B variant) — fast, (3) Llama-2 70B quantized/int4 as high-quality reference, (4) MPT-30B-instruct for long context, and (5) a smaller strong multilingual model — e.g., Bloomz or a multilingual Llama variant. We'll narrow to 3 for the actual run.

[04:50] Priya: Couple notes: Llama-3 13B is promising but we need to validate FR/DE. MPT historically struggles on legal language.
[04:58] Diego: Totally. That's why we'll include targeted evals: clause extraction precision/recall and a multilingual QA set.

[05:12] Tom: For cost we prefer quantized int8 or int4 where accuracy drop is acceptable. How big is the expected accuracy delta?
[05:20] Diego: It varies. From prior runs we saw int8 often is within 1-3% on many tasks; int4 can be 3-8% depending on model and task. For legal obligations, that delta could move you below threshold, which is why we bench both quantized and fp16 variants.

[05:48] Maya: We'll provide delta numbers in the bench report and highlight quality vs cost trade-offs per model.

[06:05] Priya: Timeline — we need a pilot demo to our legal SME by mid-July. Can we run the bench next week and have results within 10 days?
[06:15] Maya: We can run a 48-hour benchmark starting week of 2026-06-29 and deliver a report by 2026-07-10 if ZenPath provides data and infra access soon.

[06:30] Ari: Ok good. On infra: we want the final bench to be in our VPC behind our firewall. Can Redwood's private offering run in our VPC?
[06:38] Diego: Yes — Redwood Private supports customer-managed VPC with a private control plane. We'll need a short network checklist and an IAM/KMS integration step. We'll share a runbook.

[06:55] Tom: Audit/logging: we need token-level audit logs and SSO (SAML) for access.
[07:01] Maya: We support SAML SSO and we can ship audit logs to your SIEM. We'll include the SOC2 and compliance pack in the doc share.

[07:18] Speaker 1: (inaudible)

[07:30] Diego: Bench design — propose three arms: A) small fast model (e.g., Mistral 7B or LLama-3 13B int8), B) midsize quantized (Llama-2 70B int8 or int4 if feasible), C) high-quality large (non-quantized 70B-ish or Llama-3 larger variant) — run identical prompts and tasks: summary, clause extraction, question-answering, multilingual tests. We'll measure precision/recall, P50/P95 latency, tokens/sec, and cost per doc.

[08:05] Priya: We also want adversarial cases — redaction failures, tricky nested obligations. Add those to the eval set.

[08:13] Diego: Good call. Include a small subset of edge cases with human labels.

[08:25] Maya: On prompts — will ZenPath use few-shot prompt engineering or prefer to evaluate instruction-tuned variants?
[08:32] Priya: Prefer instruction-tuned out of the box; we can do a small prompt/chain-of-thought engineering phase after the first bench.

[08:45] Ari: Any limitations on model footprints for the private run? We have 8x A100 nodes and some H100 capacity in our lab.
[08:52] Diego: Perfect — that'll let us test 70B quantized and non-quantized variants. We'll provide recommended GPU mapping and batch configs. Our runtime supports KV caching and continuous batching to hit your concurrency needs.

[09:05] Tom: What's the expected setup time on our side to run the private bench? Network peering + IAM + sample data staging?
[09:13] Diego: Expect about 1-2 full days of setup with our infra team if pre-reqs are met. We'll provide a checklist: VPC peering, subnets, k8s/node sizes (if on-prem), KMS role, SSH for bench orchestration.

[09:35] Priya: For metrics, please include detailed token accounting by model and per-route cost so we can plug into our cost models.

[09:42] Maya: We'll include token-level breakdown, per-model throughput and median inference cost, plus estimated monthly run-rate at your projected volume.

[10:00] Ari: On privacy: data at rest encryption and no retention by Redwood in private deployment?
[10:06] Diego: In Private mode you can opt to prevent persistent logs leaving your VPC. For hosted evaluation we can enable short retention and E2E encryption. We'll document exact retention windows.

[10:25] Speaker 2: (crosstalk)

[10:40] Priya: Small nit — can you run a quick pilot on a tiny subset in hosted mode so we can sanity-check prompts before the big bench? A short smoke run of ~100 docs would be great.

[10:48] Maya: Yes, we usually do a hosted smoke test within 48hrs, then the private bench. We'll need your 100-doc sample (anonymized).

[11:02] Diego: Regarding evaluation rubric — we'll score extraction tasks with span-level F1, and summarization with ROUGE and a small human eval for factuality. We'll share the rubric.

[11:18] Tom: For deployment conversation downstream, we may prefer a mid-size quantized model if it meets precision, to keep latency <1s and cost manageable.

[11:26] Priya: Also curious about multilingual transfer — if we fine-tune on EN, will FR/DE improve? We might need a small multilingual fine-tune set.

[11:34] Diego: Fine-tuning helps, especially for legal phrasing in specific languages. Our Optimize team can suggest a minimal fine-tune footprint — often a few thousand examples can move the needle. We'll include guidance.

[11:50] Maya: Ok to recap next steps?
[11:54] Ari: Go ahead.

[11:56] Maya: Redwood will: 1) Send a 3-model shortlist with quantized variants and cost estimates by 2026-06-20; 2) Share benchmark harness + config and evaluation rubric by 2026-06-22; 3) Run a hosted smoke test after ZenPath provides 100 anonymized docs; 4) Coordinate private 48hr benchmark in ZenPath VPC week of 2026-06-29.

[12:25] Priya: ZenPath will: provide sample datasets (100 doc smoke + 500 doc bench set), define final SLOs (precision/recall/latency), and confirm VPC peering windows.

[12:40] Tom: We'll loop in infra and security to the runbook.

[12:44] Diego: I'll send a short network checklist and the bench playbook after this call.

[12:54] Maya: Anything else?
[13:00] Priya: One more question — do you have any pre-built legal prompt templates or chain-of-thought patterns?
[13:06] Diego: We have some internal prompt templates and extraction chains; we'll include them. But final tuning will be on your data.

[13:15] Ari: Great — set the benchmark, and we'll reconvene after the report.

[13:21] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the doc pack and calendar invite for the bench kickoff.

[13:30] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript quality: a few place names and product names might be slightly garbled (e.g., Llama -> Lama in one auto-caption). Speaker turns occasionally overlapped.
